summary: John Vincent Bellezza is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology who studied under tutor Yungdrung Tenzin and teacher Tshering Choephel. He held an attested post at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences in 2014.

John W. Pettit works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed undergraduate studies at Haverford College, earned his doctorate under Robert A. F. Thurman, and studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Lal Mani Joshi, Gunapala Dharmasiri, and Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa.

John W. Schroeder specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Educated at Los Angeles Valley College and the University of Oregon under Hee-jin Kim and doctoral supervisor Don Levi, he held posts at Oregon, the College of Wooster, and St. Mary's College of Maryland.
John W. Spellman (1934–2021) was an Indologist and historian. He held academic posts at the University of Washington (circa 1964–1967) and the University of Windsor (circa 1967–1999).

John Wilson (1804–1875) worked in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies after studying at the University of Edinburgh. He served as president of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai, vice-chancellor of the University of Mumbai, and founded Wilson College, Mumbai.

John Zavos is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. His career includes posts at the University of Manchester, where he was attested as a lecturer in South Asian studies in 2010 and as an honorary research fellow in 2026.

Join Saeki (1867–1952) specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studying under Jōchō Chihaya and at Sennyu-ji. He held posts at Horyu-ji, Kangakuin, the University of Tokyo, and the Japan Academy.
Joji Fujii is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1966 to 1974 and later held a post there from circa 1989 to 2011.

Jokai Hiraoka (1923–2011) specialized in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University, and held posts at Shuchiin University and Otemae University (circa 1966–1993).

Jon Kabat-Zinn works in religious studies and medicine. Educated at Haverford College and MIT, he studied under Philip Kapleau, Thich Nhat Hanh, and Seungsahn Haengwon, later serving at the Insight Meditation Society and the University of Massachusetts Chan Medical School.

Jonardon Ganeri is a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Cambridge, King's College London, and Oxford under Bimal Krishna Matilal. He held posts at King's College London, Nottingham, Liverpool, Sussex, Monash University, NYU, and the University of Toronto.

Jonathan A. Silk is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied at Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez, as well as at Ryukoku and Kyoto Universities. He held posts at Michigan, Western Michigan, Yale, UCLA, and Leiden University.

Jonathan C. Gold works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He has held teaching posts at the University of Vermont, Drew University (attested 2006), and Princeton University (attested 2015–2016).

Jonathan Christopher Cleary (1947–2023) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed his doctoral studies at Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi and held an instructional post at Wesleyan University.

Jonathan Geen is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed his doctorate under Phyllis Granoff at McMaster University. He has held teaching posts at McMaster University, Butler University, and the University of Rochester.

Jonathan Glover is a philosopher educated at Tonbridge School and Corpus Christi College, Oxford. His career includes posts as fellow and tutor at New College, Oxford, Distinguished Research Fellow at Oxford, and a post at King's College London.

Jonathan Lear (1948–2025) was a philosopher educated at Yale, Cambridge, Rockefeller University, and the Western New England Institute for Psychoanalysis. He held academic posts at Cambridge, Clare College, Yale University, and the University of Chicago.

Jonathan Mark Kenoyer is an archaeologist and Indologist. After attending Woodstock School, he earned his BA from the University of California, Berkeley, and joined the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where he became Professor of Anthropology circa 1985.

Jonathan Z. Smith (1938–2017) was a religious studies scholar educated at Haverford College, Yale Divinity School, and Yale University. He held positions at Dartmouth College, UC Santa Barbara, and the University of Chicago, where he was Dean of the College.

Jong-Nam Choi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Shitennoji University, he completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg under doctoral supervisor Lambert Schmithausen and studied under Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan, Albrecht Wezler, and David Seyfort Ruegg.
